blocks.prompt: 4 (a) Write down the \(n\)th term of the sequence: \(7, 13, 19, 25, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
We must find one formula \(a_n\) that gives every term when \(n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\)
The terms change by the same amount each time, so the formula has the form \(a_n = dn + c\).
Plan: find \(d\), then find \(c\) from the first term, then check.
steps:
Given: \(7, 13, 19, 25, \ldots\)
To find: the \(n\)th term \(a_n\).
Method: Equal differences \(d\) mean \(a_n = dn + c\); put \(n = 1\) to find \(c\).

Find the common difference
\[13 - 7 = 6,\ 19 - 13 = 6\]
\[25 - 19 = 6\]
Why: All the differences are \(6\), so \(a_n = 6n + c\).

Find \(c\) from the first term
\[6(1) + c = 7\]
\[c = 1\]
\[a_n = 6n + 1\]
Why: At \(n = 1\) the formula must give the first term.

Check with other terms
\[n = 2:\ 6(2) + 1 = 13 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 3:\ 6(3) + 1 = 19 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula reproduces the given terms.

blocks.prompt: 4 (b) Write down the \(n\)th term of the sequence: \(7, 4, 1, -2, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
We must find one formula \(a_n\) that gives every term when \(n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\)
The terms change by the same amount each time, so the formula has the form \(a_n = dn + c\).
Plan: find \(d\), then find \(c\) from the first term, then check.
steps:
Given: \(7, 4, 1, -2, \ldots\)
To find: the \(n\)th term \(a_n\).
Method: Equal differences \(d\) mean \(a_n = dn + c\); put \(n = 1\) to find \(c\).

Find the common difference
\[4 - 7 = -3,\ 1 - 4 = -3\]
\[-2 - 1 = -3\]
Why: All the differences are \(-3\), so \(a_n = -3n + c\).

Find \(c\) from the first term
\[-3(1) + c = 7\]
\[c = 10\]
\[a_n = -3n + 10 = 10 - 3n\]
Why: At \(n = 1\) the formula must give the first term.

Check with other terms
\[n = 2:\ 10 - 6 = 4 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 4:\ 10 - 12 = -2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula reproduces the given terms.

blocks.prompt: 4 (c) Write down the \(n\)th term of the sequence: \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{5}, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
The terms are fractions that do not change by a fixed amount.
Plan: look at the numerators and the denominators separately and compare each with the position \(n\).
steps:
Given: \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{5}, \ldots\)
To find: the \(n\)th term \(a_n\).
Method: Find the pattern of the numerators and of the denominators against the position.

Denominators against the position
\[n = 1, 2, 3, 4\]
\[\text{bottom} = 2, 3, 4, 5\]
\[\text{bottom} = n + 1\]
Why: Each denominator is one more than the position number.

Write and check
\[a_n = \dfrac{1}{n + 1}\]
\[n = 3:\ \dfrac{1}{4} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Putting \(n = 3\) gives the third term.

blocks.prompt: 4 (d) Write down the \(n\)th term of the sequence: \(-15, -4, 7, 18, \ldots\)
blocks.explanation:
We must find one formula \(a_n\) that gives every term when \(n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\)
The terms change by the same amount each time, so the formula has the form \(a_n = dn + c\).
Plan: find \(d\), then find \(c\) from the first term, then check.
steps:
Given: \(-15, -4, 7, 18, \ldots\)
To find: the \(n\)th term \(a_n\).
Method: Equal differences \(d\) mean \(a_n = dn + c\); put \(n = 1\) to find \(c\).

Find the common difference
\[-4 - (-15) = 11\]
\[7 - (-4) = 11,\ 18 - 7 = 11\]
Why: All the differences are \(11\), so \(a_n = 11n + c\).

Find \(c\) from the first term
\[11(1) + c = -15\]
\[c = -26\]
\[a_n = 11n - 26\]
Why: At \(n = 1\) the formula must give the first term.

Check with other terms
\[n = 3:\ 33 - 26 = 7 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 4:\ 44 - 26 = 18 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The formula reproduces the given terms.
